Keyboard shortcuts
TAdd text
SAdd a sticky note
DAdd today's date
EnterWith a tool picked, place it in the middle of the page (no mouse needed)
EscStep back one level: stop editing, then deselect, then back to the Select tool
← → ↑ ↓Something selected: nudge it 1 pt (hold Shift for 10 pt). Nothing selected: previous / next page
DeleteRemove the selected element
← → in the filmstripMove between page thumbnails. Hold Alt to move the page itself
↑ ↓ in the tool railMove between tools
Ctrl+C / X / VCopy, cut, paste the selected element
Ctrl+ZUndo
Ctrl+YRedo (or Ctrl+Shift+Z)
? or F1This panel

On a Mac, Cmd works wherever Ctrl is shown.

PDFEDTR edits PDFs entirely in your browser: add text, sticky notes, dates, highlights, shapes, form fields and signatures, and reorder, add or delete pages.

Private by design. The PDF you open is read into this tab and never uploaded. There is no server, no account and no analytics. Downloading writes the edited file straight to your computer.

Outside code. The online version loads two libraries - pdf.js (to draw pages) and pdf-lib (to write the edited file) - and its fonts from CDNs. The offline version, pdf-offline.html, has all of that built in and needs no network at all.

Part of a family of browser tools that all work this way - see More apps.
